output.answer: Arini Capital presented to SBCERA's Investment Committee on August 14, 2025 (and its deck was filed as Exhibit A to the Board of Retirement's September 4, 2025 agenda) in support of establishing a $200 million Master Custody Account (MCA) with Arini Capital Management. Founder Hamza Lemssouguer and Anthony Nazar de Jaucourt presented in person; the deck, titled 'San Bernardino County Employees' Retirement Association, August 14, 2025,' covered: (1) a firm overview — specialized European alternative credit manager founded October 2021, ~$9.7bn AuM, ~92 employees, London and New York offices; (2) the European credit market opportunity; (3) the Arini Credit Master Fund (ACMF), an open-ended long/short all-weather strategy, and the Arini Credit Opportunities Fund (ACOF), a drawdown catalyst-driven strategy targeting 1.8-2x MOIC and 15-20% annualized IRR (+19.63% net IRR for Fund I since December 2023 first close); and (4) case studies (long ASDA 2023/2024; short Atos 2022 and short Diebold Nixdorf 2022). The proposed MCA allocation was $50mm (25%) to ACMF, $75mm (37.5%) to ACOF and $75mm (37.5%) to direct/bespoke investments, within SBCERA's 17% Global Fixed Income target allocation (1.2% of plan assets). The Investment Committee approved it 3-1 on August 14, 2025, and the full Board of Retirement approved it on September 4, 2025, subject to completion of due diligence and legal documentation.
caveats: The presentation deck itself is largely marketing material with extensive disclaimers; its performance figures (e.g., 15-20% IRR target, back-tested data) are Arini's own and are subject to the deck's disclaimers that past performance is not indicative of future results.
The Investment Committee approval on August 14, 2025 passed 3-1 (Trustee Fiorino dissenting) and recommended an RFP discussion for new investment managers, so board support was not unanimous.
The $200M MCA approval was expressly 'subject to completion of due diligence and legal documentation,' so final terms could differ from what was presented.

output.question: What did Arini Capital present to the San Bernardino County Employees' Retirement Association?

key_facts.fact: Arini Capital founder Hamza Lemssouguer and Anthony Nazar de Jaucourt presented to SBCERA's Investment Committee on August 14, 2025 in support of establishing a Master Custody Account (MCA) with Arini Capital Management, including a $200 million initial allocation; the committee approved 3-1 (Basle, Stafford, Newcomer ayes; Fiorino nay).

The Board of Retirement approved the $200M Arini MCA on September 4, 2025, subject to completion of due diligence and legal documentation; the agenda item (File #25-294.1) attached Exhibit A: Arini Capital Presentation and Exhibit B: NEPC Cover Memo.

The proposed MCA had three sleeves: $50mm (25%) to the Arini Credit Master Fund (open-ended long/short all-weather strategy across public bonds, loans, CDS and structured credit, mostly Europe); $75mm (37.5%) to the Arini Credit Opportunities Fund (drawdown, catalyst-driven, 50/50 public/private); and $75mm (37.5%) to direct/bespoke investments, mostly private opportunities in Europe.

Arini's presentation deck (Exhibit A, dated August 14, 2025) covered: firm overview (founder Hamza Lemssouguer, c.$9.7bn AuM as of June 30, 2025, ~92 employees, London/New York offices, launched Jan-22); market opportunity in European credit; ACMF and ACOF strategies and performance; and case studies (long ASDA 2023/2024; short Atos 2022; short Diebold Nixdorf 2022).

In the deck, ACOF targeted 1.8-2x MOIC and 15-20% annualized IRR, with Fund I having generated +19.63% net IRR since its December 2023 first close; the staff report stated staff and NEPC expect the blended portfolio to achieve a low double-digit to mid-teens net return over a typical cycle.

The investment was to be included in SBCERA's Global Fixed Income allocation (17% board-established target of plan assets), with the $200mm initial commitment equal to 1.2% of plan assets and potential for account growth pending additional co-invest and strategy-specific diligence.

The MCA stemmed from a 2024 effort to broaden SBCERA's European credit capabilities: staff surveyed 62 managers, conducted focused diligence on 10, and identified 4 managers aligned with SBCERA's objectives.
